en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty The Twentieth Chapter
The Discourse on the Wardens of Hell:
"Are there no wardens of hell in the hells?
"Yes, [there are]."
Is it not the case that there are no tortures in the hells?
One should certainly not say so... [etc.
... Is it the case that there are tortures in the hells?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Are there hell-wardens in the hells?
You should not say so … [and so on] …
Is there, among humans, both the infliction of punishment and the one who inflicts it?
Yes. Is there, in the hells, both the infliction of punishment and the one who inflicts it?
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is it the case that there are punishments for deeds in the hells, yet no one who inflicts those punishments?
Yes, it is.
Is it the case that among humans there are those who inflict punishment, yet no one who is punished?
One should not say so… [and so on]… Is it the case that in the hells there are hell-guardians?
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “Has it not been said by the Blessed One:
‘Neither Vessabhū nor even Pettirāja...’?”
Soma, Yama, and King Vessavaṇa—
there they destroy their own deeds,
having been driven from here and arrived in the other world.
Is that indeed the Sutta? Yes.
Therefore, there are no hell-guardians in the hells.
"There are no hell-wardens in the hells"?
"Yes.
But was it not said by the Blessed One:
“Monks, the wardens of hell subject him to a torture called the fivefold binding:
they drive a red-hot iron stake through his right hand, they drive a red-hot iron stake through his second hand,
they drive a red-hot iron stake through his foot, they drive a red-hot iron stake through his second foot, and they drive a red-hot iron stake through the middle of his chest.”
"There he experiences painful, sharp, and bitter sensations;
yet he does not die as long as that evil kamma has not been exhausted.
Is this indeed a sutta?
“Yes,” he replied.
“In that case, there are wardens in the hells.
Is it not the case that there are wardens in the hells?”
“Yes, [they do].
“But was it not said by the Blessed One:
‘Then, monks, the wardens of hell, having laid him down, pare him with axes...’?”
“Monks, the wardens of hell place that person with his feet up and his head down and pare him with axes...
Monks, the wardens of hell yoke that person to a chariot and drive him back and forth over ground that is burning, blazing, and glowing...
Monks, the wardens of hell make that person ascend and descend a great mountain of embers that is burning, blazing, and glowing...”
Then, monks, the wardens of hell seize him, turn him upside down with his feet up and head down, and cast him into a heated iron cauldron—blazing, flaming, and glowing.
There he is cooked, submerged in a mass of froth; while being cooked there, submerged in that mass of froth, he goes up at one moment, down at another, and sideways at another.
There he experiences painful, sharp, and bitter sensations, yet he does not die as long as that evil karma has not been exhausted.
Then, monks, the wardens of hell throw him into the Great Hell.
Now, monks, that Great Hell has four corners and four gates.
It is divided and measured into portions;
it has a perimeter of iron walls and is covered over with iron.
For him, the ground is made of iron,
blazing and filled with heat,
extending for a hundred leagues in every direction.
“Having pierced through, it remains forever.
Is this indeed a sutta?
Yes, it is.
Therefore, there are indeed guardians of hell in the hells.
The discussion on the guardians of hell is finished.
